title: If you will (Mark 1:40–45)
hookLine: a man with leprosy says if you are willing; Jesus, moved, touches him

lines: OUTSIDE THE TOWN, CALLING A WARNING.
HE KNEELS IN FRONT OF JESUS.
cards: A handshake, a hug, a hand on a shoulder: small touches nobody counts until they stop. For the man in today's story, they had stopped.
He had a skin disease the Bible calls leprosy, and the law said he had to live outside the town, clothes torn, calling out a warning so nobody came near. Nobody touched him. Nobody was supposed to.
Then one day, breaking every rule of distance, he walks straight up to Jesus and kneels.

teach.b: Leper is the old word for a person with leprosy. Some people now prefer to say a person with leprosy, because leper came to mean an outcast, and this man was one.
In the Bible, leprosy covers a range of skin diseases, not only what doctors now call Hansen's disease.

Leviticus says such a person "shall cry, Unclean, unclean," and "he shall dwell alone; without the camp shall his habitation be." He asks, in the King James Bible: "If thou wilt, thou canst make me clean."
He's sure Jesus can. His question is whether Jesus wants to.

teach.h: NOT CAN YOU, BUT DO YOU WANT TO.
teach.b: That's the question under a lot of human pain: not is it possible, but does anyone want to? Then Mark: "And Jesus, moved with compassion, put forth his hand, and touched him, and saith unto him, I will; be thou clean."
And before a word of healing, a touch, while the man is still unclean by the law's own terms. Under the purity laws, uncleanness could pass by touch.

Mark tells it the other way round: Jesus touches, and the man is made clean. A few old manuscripts say not moved with compassion, but moved with anger. Anger at the disease, perhaps, or at his isolation.
Scholars still debate which reading is original.
Jesus tells the man to tell no one, and to show himself to the priest as the law required. The man tells everyone. Now Jesus can't openly enter a town; he stays out in the lonely places.
The outsider comes in, and Jesus ends up outside.

how: Many Christians take this story as a call to reach people who are isolated, and Christian groups have long run hospitals and missions for people with leprosy and other stigmatized illnesses.

games.q: a man with leprosy kneels in front of you, against every rule of distance, and says: if you are willing, you can make me clean. what does Jesus do?
o: step back and heal him with a word from a distance.
reach out and touch him, and say I will.
tell him to go to the priest first.
games.why: "put forth his hand, and touched him, and saith unto him, I will; be thou clean." the touch came first, while the man was still unclean.

practice: Rest one hand on your own shoulder, or over your heart, and notice what a kind touch feels like.
Then hold the face of someone who may not have been touched kindly in a while: an older neighbor, a friend living alone, someone grieving, someone everyone keeps at a distance.
If you pray, pray for them by name; if you don't, just wish them well, and think of one appropriate, kind touch you could offer: a handshake, a hug, a hand on a shoulder.
